summary: Svalbard Airport, Longyear (LYR) is the northernmost airport in the world with scheduled public flights, located at 78° North latitude on the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard, Norway. It serves as the primary gateway to Longyearbyen, supporting Arctic tourism, scientific research, and the local community of around 2,500 residents. The airport operates under extreme polar conditions, including polar night darkness in winter and midnight sun in summer.
faqs:
Q: What is the northernmost airport with regular flights?
A: Svalbard Airport, Longyear (LYR) holds this distinction at approximately 78° North latitude.

Q: Which airlines operate from Svalbard Airport?
A: Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) and Norwegian Air Shuttle provide scheduled flights, mainly to Tromsø and Oslo.

Q: How far is the airport from Longyearbyen town center?
A: The airport is approximately 3 kilometers from the town center, roughly a 10-minute drive.

Q: Does the airport operate year-round?
A: Yes, Svalbard Airport operates year-round despite extreme Arctic weather conditions and polar night darkness.
transport_tips: Taxis and airport shuttles are available at the terminal for the short transfer into Longyearbyen, typically taking around 10 minutes. Rental cars and pre-booked transfers should be arranged in advance, especially during peak tourism seasons. During winter, road conditions can be icy, so confirm transport pickup times with your provider.
local_tip: Always carry bear protection and inform someone of your travel plans when leaving Longyearbyen, as polar bears are present on Svalbard and can appear near settlements and roads.
